get.description: [native] Liveness, for any caller: `status` (healthy|degraded), and HTTP 503 when PostgreSQL or NATS is down. `engine`, `version`, `peers`, `dependencies` and `addons` are returned ONLY to a caller that presents a credential — they describe the deployment, and an anonymous probe needs the status code, not the inventory.

addons.description: Opt-in subsystem states, keyed by add-on name (`trellion`, `evolve`, `trellion_intel`, …). Built from the gateway's `addons::ADDONS` table, so a new add-on appears here with no schema change — clients must render the keys they receive rather than a fixed list. Three of the four states are emitted today by `addons::health_word`: `enabled`; `disabled`, meaning the operator turned it off, which is NOT a fault; and `unlicensed`, meaning the flag is on but no entitlement grants it, which is also not a fault but needs an action the operator can take (`noo security entitlement install <token>`). The per-add-on reason is deliberately NOT carried here — /health is polled by the compose healthcheck and the host watcher on a short interval, and operator prose on every poll costs bandwidth continuously for something only a human reading a console needs. `unhealthy` (flag on, container missing or down) IS a fault and is specced but NOT YET EMITTED — no arm of `health_word` produces it. Treat any unrecognised value as unknown rather than guessing.

[native] A node-agent pushes a batch of its OWN log lines; the gateway stamps every stream's `node` label with the caller's verified node id (the body's `node` is never believed), keeps only the labels `source`, `name`, `stream`, `level`, `compose_service` (others dropped), and relays the batch to Loki `POST /loki/api/v1/push` with the gateway's own leaf. NODE route: a node cluster credential (client cert + fleet token) for `{node_id}` itself; an operator JWT, a service key or a stack service on the controller secret gets 403. Body is the Loki push shape, JSON, optionally `Content-Encoding: gzip`. Limits: 4 MB on the wire and decoded (413), 64 streams and 20 000 entries per push, 8 labels per stream, 128 bytes per label value (400); per node 8 MB and 120 pushes a minute (429 + Retry-After; `NOO_LOGS_INGEST_BYTES_PER_MIN`, `NOO_LOGS_INGEST_REQUESTS_PER_MIN`). Shipper contract: 204 = accepted, drop the batch; 400/413 = malformed, drop it; 403 = credential, keep it; 429 = wait Retry-After; 503 = Loki down/unconfigured, keep it and retry with backoff. The gateway buffers nothing. Every refusal body is `{error, reason, retry}`. Not written to the gateway's access log (self-loop).

[delegated] Changes which audience documents belong to (via NATS worker.rag.retag). Select with `match` (a glob on source_uri) or `doc_ids`; an empty selector is refused rather than meaning everything. `only_untagged` defaults true, so backfilling an unclassified document and overwriting a classification somebody chose stay separate acts. Dry-run unless `apply` is true: the response reports what WOULD change. Target roles are clamped to what the requester could write to itself, and a refused role is named rather than dropped. `roles` must be non-empty: a document always has an audience (an empty list is refused; use `admin` to make one admin-only). Every applied retag appends {at, by, from, to} to each changed document's `metadata.audience_history` (last 20) and writes a `kb_retag` row to the security audit log.

**BREAKING: operation-backed route.** Starts an asynchronous operation (`GET /api/v1/ops/types`) and waits up to this type's default wait (`?wait=` overrides). Finished in time: `200` with the result in the shape and status this route has always answered. Otherwise `202` with an `OperationHandle`; poll `GET /api/v1/ops/{op_id}?wait=` for the result. Callers MUST handle both answers. Default wait: 3 s. . [delegated] Ingests a document into the knowledge base (via NATS worker.rag.ingest).

200.description: Finished within the wait: the result, in the route's historical shape.

202.description: The run outlasted its wait: an operation handle to poll.

parameters.name: wait
parameters.description: Seconds to hold the request for the operation before answering with its handle (overrides the type's default wait; `0` always answers with the handle; at most 25).

get.description: [native] Returns RAG system status (table counts, embedding stats).

[native] Returns documents in the knowledge base, newest first, paged by limit (default 200, max 2000) and offset. Operators and admins also get `roles` per item (audience tags; null = untagged). A caller who is not unrestricted (admin) sees only documents their audience may read — own `user:<account>`, `company`, `system` and granted `team:*`; untagged documents are admin-only — the same set retrieval uses. With summary=true the body is instead {docs: [...], summary: {total, untagged, by_audience}} with the counts taken over every document the caller may read, not just the page. Operators and admins also get `provenance` ({by, via, at} of the first ingest; null = ingested before provenance was recorded) and `audience_history_len`. Four filters narrow the listing AND the summary: `untagged`, `audience` (a tag; a trailing `*` is a prefix, so `user:*` is every personal tier), `match` (a glob on source_uri, the dialect `rag/retag` takes) and `q` (title substring, case-insensitive). Each is ANDed with the caller's audience, so a filter can only remove rows.

provenance.description: Operator/admin: where the document came from ({by, via, at}); null = unknown.

audience_history_len.description: Operator/admin: how many times the audience was changed (last 20 kept).

parameters.name: untagged
parameters.description: Only documents with no audience tag.

parameters.name: audience
parameters.description: Only documents whose audience contains this tag; a trailing `*` is a prefix (`user:*` = any personal tier).

parameters.name: match
parameters.description: Only documents whose source_uri matches this glob (`*`, `?`), as `rag/retag` takes.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Only documents whose title contains this text, case-insensitively.

[native] Operator-only. Changes ONLY the task's cron `schedule` (and `updated_at`); name, action, config, channels, recipients and enabled are untouched, unlike re-creating the task with POST /api/heartbeat/tasks, which replaces the whole row. The cron is validated with the parser the scheduler fires from (400 with its reason when it does not parse). `next_run` is cleared when the schedule actually changes, so the tick loop reseats it; an unchanged schedule leaves it alone. A destructive task's schedule edited without a person's own credential is filed as a proposal instead (`proposal: true`) and nothing changes. 404 for an unknown task.

get.description: [native] Returns autonomy engine status and active locations. `enabled` and `running` are DIFFERENT facts and must not be collapsed: `enabled` is whether the engine is permitted to act, `running` is whether its loop is actually ticking. Reporting the first as the second is the 'the loop died and nobody noticed' failure the gateway's loop_health registry exists to catch.

running.description: The engine's loop is actually alive, per loop_health liveness.

armed.description: Whether this location's ACTION is armed. OMITTED for a location with no gate - absent means 'no gate exists', a different fact from false ('its gate is off'). Render absence as unknown, never as off.

dry_run.description: Second opt-in on destructive actions: armed but dry_run still takes no action. Omitted, like armed, when the location has no gate.

last_fired.description: RFC3339 of the last time this location FIRED, from the audit table (survives restart). Null means unknown, NOT never.

post.description: Proposal 49. One transaction: revoke every active key for `consumer` AND disable the bound account. Revoking the key stops the next mint; disabling the account is what reaches a token ALREADY IN FLIGHT, because the auth layer re-checks the subject of a delegated token on every request (~10s cache). Doing these as two client calls has a failure mode with no good half — revoke succeeds, disable fails, and the operator is told "revoked" while a live token keeps working. Refuses an unbound (machine) key: there is no account to disable, and degrading to a plain revoke would mean the button did half of what its name says — use `/revoke` for those. Takes the same clamps as the standalone verbs: `may_manage` over the account, and the last-admin guard.

post.summary: Exchange a provisioning key for a short-lived token acting as one account
post.description: Proposal 49 — OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange (RFC 8693) in its administrative-issuance profile. Bearer = a service key issued with scope `identity` and BOUND to an account (`noo security service-key issue <name> --scopes identity --user <account>`); an unbound key is refused, because the subjects it may mint for are decided from the bound account's tier. The middleware resolves the key ONLY on this route. `subject_token` is the identity to act as. Two subject types: `urn:noomesh:params:oauth:token-type:account` (the default — a mesh account, entitled by `may_manage`) and `urn:noomesh:params:oauth:token-type:connection` (one live session, `<account>/<label>`, entitled by the issuer OWNING the name — deliberately NOT `may_manage`, which asks a different question). A connection may not mint another connection: it is a leaf, and a client needing a new one re-authenticates with the provisioning credential. Both are noomesh-defined: the subject is asserted by the issuer, not presented by the subject. `grant_type`, when sent, must be `urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange`. Returns an ORDINARY user JWT for that account — no new trust class — carrying a signed RFC 8693 §4.1 `act` claim naming the provisioning key and its bound account. The minted role is the LOWER of the subject's live tier and the issuer's, and `may_manage` refuses a subject at or above the issuer's tier outright. Default TTL 300s, clamped to [60, 3600]. There is no `on_behalf_of` request field and deliberately so: a shared credential must not be able to name an arbitrary subject. A minted token is stateless and cannot be revoked before it expires — revoking the key stops new mints, disabling the account stops the next one. Requires the `identity` add-on, which is free and on by default. Quota'd by the key's `rpm_limit`.

post.summary: Open Grafana as the noomesh account at the browser
post.description: an earlier change. Mints a short-lived Grafana session token for the LIVE noomesh account behind the login and returns the URL to open Grafana with (`<GRAFANA_ROOT_URL>/?auth_token=<jwt>`; Grafana's `[auth.jwt] url_login`). Any authenticated login: the account is RE-READ from `noo_users` (a disabled or deleted account is refused with 403), and its live tier - never the access token's `role` claim - becomes the token's `role`, and its Grafana org role from `auth::GRAFANA_ORG_ROLES` (the one tier->role table: admin->Admin, operator->Editor, user->Viewer, dashboards only) becomes `grafana_role`, which grafana.ini passes through. The token is ES256 with a DEDICATED key pair (`${NOO_PKI_DIR}/sso/grafana.key`; `noo security pki issue-sso-key`), `aud = noo-grafana`, no `kid`; the gateway itself refuses it. Grafana JWT auth is stateless, so the token IS the session: `NOO_GRAFANA_SESSION_TTL` minutes (5 default, 60 max), and no Grafana session outlives it - a disabled account's open tab dies at `expires_at`. 503 with the fix when `NOO_GRAFANA_URL` (`GRAFANA_ROOT_URL`) or the key is absent. Exchanged (`act`), harness, kiosk and add-on tokens, service keys and the cluster HMAC are refused (403): a person has to be at the browser. One audit row per mint (`grafana_session_issued`). The console opens the URL in a new tab; when it expires the person clicks Open Grafana again.

The fleet search behind `noo logs search` and the MCP `noo_logs_search`: "what happened on host3 at 14:02" (`node`, `since`, `until`), "every error in the last hour" (`level`, `since`). The gateway BUILDS the LogQL from the typed fields — a selector over the shipped labels `node`, `name`, `source`, `level` and a `|=` line filter for `text` with `"` and `\` escaped, so no field can open a pipeline stage. A `query` starting with `{` is an operator's own LogQL and passes through unchanged (the raw door `/api/logs/query` already opens that), under the same caps: `limit` <= 2000 and a window of at most 7 days (`range_clamped` says when `since` was moved). A `query` not starting with `{` is free text. The answer names the LogQL used. No fallback: Loki unconfigured or down is 503 with the reason, because a node-agent scan cannot answer a fleet query honestly; a Loki-refused query is 400 with Loki's text.

post.description: **Operation-backed route.** Starts an asynchronous operation (type `graph.entity_cleanup`, `GET /api/v1/ops/types`) and waits up to its default wait, 3 s (`?wait=` overrides). Finished in time: `200` with the report. Otherwise `202` with an `OperationHandle`; poll `GET /api/v1/ops/{op_id}?wait=`. Callers MUST handle both answers. . Restorable for the staging retention window (30 days) with `POST /api/v1/graph/prune/restore`. **ADMIN ONLY**, and an apply needs a person's own credential: a harness credential (the MCP operator door) may preview but gets `403` on `apply: true`, naming `noo graph entity-cleanup --apply` (an Operator, a User, a controller service and a worker-delegated agent token are refused `403`, here and at `POST /api/v1/ops`). **Dry run by default**: with `apply` absent or false only SELECTs run and nothing is audited. An applied run writes `graph_entity_cleanup` security-audit rows (`started` before the worker is asked, then `ok`/`busy`/`failed`) holding the actor, counts and `run_id`, never an entity name; if the first cannot be written nothing is deleted (`503`). Delegated to `worker.rag.entity_cleanup` (the open `ml` surface; requires a trellion build that ships `trellion.live.junk_entity_cleanup`, else a clear upgrade error) on a 600 s timeout. At most `max_delete` (default and ceiling 5000) entities per applied run; run again to continue. Refused as busy (`409`, a failed op) while graph prune or a recluster holds the graph.

apply.description: true = stage and delete; absent or false = dry run

examples.description: how many of the most-connected junk entities to list

max_delete.description: most entities one applied run removes

400.description: A parameter is out of range or `apply` is not a boolean

403.description: Not an Admin (an Operator, a User, a service credential or an agent token)

409.description: Busy: graph prune or a recluster is running; nothing was changed

503.description: The audit row could not be written, so nothing was deleted; or the trellion add-on is off

get.description: [native] GET /api/heartbeat/review-existing — the existing tasks (full config) and saved recipients that no person has approved: an agent-turn, destructive or delivering task with no `authorised_by`, and a saved recipient with no `created_by`. Until reviewed, the tasks run read-only and their targets are not registered.

post.description: [native] POST /api/heartbeat/review-existing/approve — body `{tasks: [id], recipients: [id]}`. A person only (no harness claim, no `act`, an enabled account): each task is recorded as authorised by them and each recipient as created by them. A task that needs a higher role than theirs is skipped and named.

get.description: [native] GET /api/security/user-proposals/{id}

post.description: [native] Moves an EVOLVED skill's file into a `graveyard/` directory beside it, which removes it from selection and the listing. A core skill is refused. Operator-gated by the global write rule; also opened by the `prompt_skills:write` scope.

400.description: The skill is core (`{"error":"core skills are never mutated"}`), or the body is invalid.

post.summary: Adjust an evolved prompt skill's fitness
post.description: [native] Adds `delta` to an EVOLVED skill's fitness, clamps the result to 0..10 and persists it. A negative delta that lands on 0 retires the skill (`retired: true`). A core skill is refused. Operator-gated by the global write rule; also opened by the `prompt_skills:write` scope.

400.description: The skill is core (`{"error":"core skills are never mutated"}`), or the body is invalid.

get.description: [native] GET /api/cluster/model-classes — the live class table: declared and derived classes with every candidate's status (`placed` / `available` / `unplaced`) and health, plus the aliases. What `noo cluster class list` prints and the `model classes` row of `noo cluster verify` judges.

put.description: [native] PUT /api/cluster/model-classes/{class} — declare (replace) a class: `{candidates: [{node, backend, model?, degraded?}], aliases?: [..]}`. `model` omitted = the placement's model on that node. Operator role (every non-GET under `/api/cluster` is).

delete.description: [native] DELETE /api/cluster/model-classes/{class} — forget a declaration (and its aliases). The derived class of the same model, if any, takes over.

get.description: [native] GET /api/v1/docs/held?reason=&limit=&offset= — held documents (id, title, reason, held_at), paged, with the `total`. Operator only.

post.description: [native] POST /api/v1/docs/hold — keep documents, out of embedding and search. Body `{title_prefix | doc_ids, reason, apply}`. A DRY RUN unless `apply` is `true`: the answer says what WOULD be held. Nothing is deleted.

[native] POST /api/v1/docs/purge — DELETE the documents held under exactly `reason`. IRREVERSIBLE. Body `{reason, apply}`; a dry run unless `apply` is `true`. Documents that are not held, or held under another reason, are never touched.
[native] POST /api/v1/docs/unhold — release held documents (same body as hold, no reason needed). A dry run unless `apply` is `true`.
[native] POST /api/cluster/nodes/{node_id}/fit — read-only memory-fit verdict for the node's placements, optionally with one more (`noo cluster fit`). Changes nothing.

get.description: [native] GET /api/alerts/list[?state=firing|pending|inactive&alertmanager=true] — every alerting rule with its state, severity, summary, `activeAt` and `for`, firing first, merged from Prometheus `/api/v1/rules` and `/api/v1/alerts`. Alertmanager's own view (active, silenced, inhibited) is added under `alertmanager` unless `alertmanager=false`; if Alertmanager cannot be reached that section reports the error and the Prometheus half still answers. Read-only: nothing here silences or acknowledges.

[native] GET /api/metrics/discover[?label=&selector=&prefix=&limit=] — what can I ask Prometheus for? With no `label`, the metric names (`__name__`); with one, that label's values (for example `job` or `instance`). `selector` is a series selector narrowing the lookup (`{job="node"}`), `prefix` filters by leading characters, results are sorted and capped at 500.
[native] GET /api/metrics/range?query=<PromQL>&start=&end=&step= — Prometheus `query_range` proxy (operator-only, read-only).

get.summary: The controller's own node id and the birth cert fingerprint the rail verifies it against
get.description: [native] GET /api/cluster/self-node — the controller's own node id and the DER-sha256 fingerprint of the birth cert the gateway verifies its fetch receipts and apply reports against (i67). Read-only: the cert is a host file, and nothing here can change it. `noo cluster provision <self>` compares the fingerprint with `/etc/noo/birth.crt` before staging.

post.description: [native] Answer the question a task asked: a new loop starts with the question and the answer.
[native] Ask the task's owner a question the loop cannot go on without: posted to its thread; the task waits for the answer from the next loop boundary.
[native] Give a task more tokens: a task parked because its budget ran out resumes from its checkpoint; on a running task only its cap changes.

get.description: [native] GET /api/usage/me — one person's spend this period: node, cloud and per-harness-kind columns (never merged), the allowance and what is left, and cost_usd per column.
[native] GET /api/users/{username}/allowance — a person's token allowance and its use this period (Admin, or the person).

put.description: [native] PUT /api/users/{username}/allowance — set a person's standing token allowance per period (Admin): body {tokens, period?=month}.

delete.description: [native] DELETE /api/users/{username}/allowance — remove a person's allowance: no standing cap (Admin).

get.description: [native] GET /api/security/audit/list

post.description: [native] POST /api/cluster/seat-enroll — redeem a seat token.

get.description: [native] GET /api/cluster/seat-tokens — issuance metadata, never hashes.

post.description: [native] POST /api/cluster/seat-tokens — mint a one-time seat enrolment token.
[native] POST /api/cluster/seat-tokens/{id}/revoke — idempotent.

get.description: [native] GET /api/cluster/seats — every enrolled seat with its last heartbeat and the state of its staged bundle. What `noo upgrade` and `noo cluster verify` read, and the ONLY place either learns a seat exists.

post.description: [native] POST /api/cluster/seats/{seat}/bundle — stage a seat's bundle: CMS ciphertext to the seat's birth cert, built and signed by the controller's CLI. Upsert; the seat's sync timer collects it.

get.description: [native] GET /api/cluster/seats/{seat}/status — the staged bundle and the seat's receipts, the same shape as a node's provision-bundle status so the CLI's combined wait judges both with one function.

post.description: [native] POST /bootstrap/seat/{seat}/applied — `{sha, rc, msg}`, signed.

get.description: [native] GET /bootstrap/seat/{seat}/bundle — the seat collects its ciphertext. The GET is SIGNED (unlike a node's, which happens before the node holds anything): a seat is fully enrolled before it ever fetches.

post.description: [native] POST /bootstrap/seat/{seat}/fetched — `{sha}`, signed. Stamps fetched_at.

[native] POST /bootstrap/seat/{seat}/heartbeat — the seat's state (CLI version, kiosk units, console build), signed over the sha256 of the exact body bytes so a captured proof cannot carry a different body.

[native] Operator hold on a node's GPU: pause its GPU backends now and keep them paused (no automatic resume) until a release. For handing the GPU to work outside noomesh that will not start while the GPU is occupied.
[native] End an operator GPU hold: the node returns to the automatic shared-GPU policy and resumes its GPU backends once the GPU has stayed free.

get.description: [native] GET /api/cluster/nodes/{node_id}/control-probe

post.description: [native] Measure a node's chat model: the gateway asks the node agent's `POST /bench`, which loads the model, times a reference prefill and decode, keeps the result and reports it as `model_bench` on every heartbeat after. The answer is that `model_bench` object (`{model, backend, load_secs, prefill_tps, decode_tps, prompt_tokens, at}`); the node's resolved harness profile (`desired-config`) derives its `first_byte_secs` from it. Operator only; audited. Up to 900 s.

get.description: [native] GET /api/cluster/embedding-spaces — every space, its model and its pool.

put.description: [native] PUT /api/cluster/embedding-spaces/{space} — declare a space (`{model, dims?}`). A new space is fine; an existing one keeps its model (changing it is a re-embed, refused with 409), and may have `dims` filled in.

delete.description: [native] DELETE /api/cluster/embedding-spaces/{space} — forget a space. The default space cannot be removed: every unqualified embed means it.

OperationHandle.description: What an operation-backed route answers 202 with when the run outlasted its wait, and what POST /api/v1/ops answers. Poll `poll` (GET, optionally `?wait=<s>`, at most 25).

joined.description: Present and true when this request joined the same account's run already in flight (exclusive types) and started nothing new.

Operation.description: One asynchronous operation as GET /api/v1/ops/{id} shows it. `result` and `result_status` appear once it has finished; a listing omits them.

params.description: As stored: ingest text is omitted, over-large params replaced by a marker.

result.description: The route's own body, in its own shape.

result_status.description: The HTTP status the synchronous route would have answered.

cancel.description: Present on a cancelled op: {gateway_aborted, worker_stopped, note}. `worker_stopped` is false: a worker run already underway is not stopped.

retry_safe.description: On a failed op: whether resubmitting is harmless.
